title: Selective Hydration Priority Queue Simulator
problemStatement: Implement `createHydrationScheduler(chunks)` that hydrates chunks in background order unless a user click event occurs on a specific chunk, which immediately elevates that chunk to the front of the hydration queue.
interviewTrap: In traditional SSR, the user must wait for the entire page to hydrate before any button responds. React 18 Selective Hydration intercepts clicks on un-hydrated islands and hydrates them synchronously before dispatching the event.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is Selective Hydration in React 18?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In traditional SSR, hydration was all-or-nothing: the browser had to download all JavaScript and hydrate the entire page before ANY component became interactive. In React 18, wrapping components in `<Suspense>` breaks the page into independent hydration chunks. React streams HTML first, and hydrates components as their JS scripts download. If a user clicks on an unhydrated component, React **prioritizes hydrating that specific component first**, making it interactive immediately!
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Core React 18 SSR streaming architecture question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Hydrating the 'Buy Now' button immediately when the user clicks it, even if the heavy 'Reviews' component further down the page is still downloading.

howToExplain.opening: Selective Hydration allows React to stream HTML progressively and prioritize hydrating the specific components the user interacts with first.
keyPoints: Suspense boundaries define independent hydration islands.
User interactions (clicks) boost hydration priority for target subtrees.
Eliminates TTI (Time to Interactive) bottlenecks on heavy pages.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Selective Hydration bridges the gap between fast server rendering and instant user interactivity.
analogies: An amusement park: instead of waiting for all 50 rides to be inspected before opening the park gates, the most popular roller coaster opens first so guests can start riding immediately.

commonMistakes.mistake: Believing hydration must wait for all Suspense boundaries to resolve.
commonMistakes.why: React hydrates each Suspense boundary independently as soon as its code and data arrive.
commonMistakes.correct: State that Suspense boundaries decouple hydration across the tree.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is Event Replaying in Selective Hydration?
followUpDeepDive.answer: If a user clicks a button before its hydration completes, React intercepts and queues the event, prioritizes hydrating that button, and then REPLAYS the click event on the newly hydrated component.
